intro: India's main animal welfare law. It makes cruelty to animals an offence and is the parent law for the Animal Birth Control (ABC) Rules, 2023, which govern stray dogs. Supreme Court orders in November 2025 and May 2026 changed how stray dogs in public places are handled — see the last chapter.

sections.t: Duty of people in charge of animals
sections.p: Anyone who owns or is in charge of an animal must take all reasonable steps to ensure its wellbeing and prevent unnecessary pain or suffering.

Includes beating, kicking, overloading or torturing an animal; giving it poison or harmful substances; keeping it in a cage too small to move in; keeping it chained for long periods; not giving it enough food, water or shelter; abandoning it where it's likely to suffer; and using animals for fighting or baiting.
sections.pen: Fine ₹10–50 for a first offence; ₹25–100 and/or up to 3 months for a repeat within 3 years
k: These penalties are very low because they date from 1960 — serious harm is usually also charged under BNS S 325
Humane slaughter for food and specified procedures are exempt

sections.p: Under the criminal code, killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animal is a separate offence of mischief — this is what police use for poisoning or killing dogs, cats, cattle and other animals.
Every citizen has a fundamental duty to have compassion for living creatures. Courts often cite this in animal cases.

Local bodies (municipalities, corporations, panchayats) must run Animal Birth Control programmes: catch stray dogs, sterilise them, vaccinate them against rabies and mark them. The rules made under S 38 of this Act replaced the 2001 rules.

The ABC Rules say sterilised dogs are to be returned to the same area they were caught from. The Supreme Court has since ordered that dogs picked up from public places must not be released back there — see the Supreme Court chapter.

The ABC Rules make residents' welfare associations and apartment bodies responsible for arranging feeding spots for community animals, away from children's play areas, entry and exit points and staircases. Feeders shouldn't be harassed for feeding at designated spots. Feeding outside such spots, in public places, is being restricted under the Supreme Court's directions.

Complaints about stray dogs (aggressive dogs, bites, sterilisation) go to your local body — in Tamil Nadu, the corporation, municipality or panchayat. Complaints about cruelty go to the police or the local Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA).

In a case it took up on its own in July 2025 after reports of dog bites and rabies deaths, the Supreme Court in November 2025 ordered stray dogs to be removed from public institutional areas — such as schools, hospitals, bus stands and railway stations — and moved to shelters after sterilisation and vaccination, instead of being released back there.
k: Applies to all states and union territories

sections.p: On 19 May 2026, the Supreme Court refused to recall the November 2025 order, holding that the right to life includes moving freely without fear of dog attacks. It allowed euthanasia of rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous dogs, after assessment by veterinary experts and following the PCA Act and ABC Rules. States must set up at least one Animal Birth Control centre per district, build shelters, and keep anti-rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin available at government hospitals. High Courts monitor compliance.
k: Officials acting in good faith under these directions are protected from criminal cases
Authorities are to consider extending the directions to other crowded public places
